kept.reason: Checks that each failed store call (Claim, Renew, DeadLetters, ...) reaches the worker as Error::Store with that call's error. a_worker_claims_heartbeats_and_finishes_a_task checks the happy path of claim, heartbeat and finish: no assertion there injects a store error, and the flaky per-call loop would change what it checks. No assertion maps; the setups conflict.

Checks that starting a process again with the same key and other input is refused key_reused, and after it ends is refused ended, with the call made once. a_process_runs_to_completion checks only completion, status paid and one charge under the step's key: none of its assertions checks a second start. Folding the restart assertions into it would put two guarantees in one scenario, against lib.rs's one home per guarantee, and hide which one failed; it would save under 10ms of world setup.

Checks that a checkout over LIMIT ends Failed(declined) and its order is compensated to cancelled. a_process_runs_to_completion checks a checkout under the limit completes and is paid: no assertion maps, and the setups conflict (one amount is declined, the other charged), so one test cannot hold both.

Remaining smells are internal and small (process_state pass-through, record's 7 args), not worth a change at this churn.

Already deep: its interface is open/path plus the Store trait (SPEC §3), a real seam with two adapters (memory, sqlite). The rules every store shares (claim_row, wake_row, release_row, check_unit, check_batch) already moved to factum-store in factum#14/#15; what remains is SQL only (schema steps, row codecs, generated projection tables, claim query), the knowledge this adapter exists to hide. Tests cross only the engine API, plus the SPEC-sanctioned file-format test. Splitting the file would move lines, not add depth.

Deep already: four public task calls (claim_task, heartbeat, finish_task, cancel_task) and five crate entries tick calls (advance_due, deliver, run_due, expire_waits, arrived) hide leases, retry/at-most-once, key pacing, lost-race retry and wait-before-row answers. Every row kind runs through one claim/drain loop and ends through one end_attempt/answer_step path; fault naming lives in item(). Tests cross only the engine API. Splitting by row kind would move lines, not add depth; remaining smells (answer_step's 7 args, a repeated Step::Await rebuild in advance_one) are local and small.
